propositions: An errored pair is counted as a decision flip when the synthetic decision (dropped) differs from the other arm's verdict, despite errored records not being model verdicts.

The flip comprehension at parity.py:107 compares decisions with no errored guard, while errored pairs are admitted to gold_pairs by label membership at parity.py:105, creating a double-count of runtime errors under both criterion (b) and criterion (d).
A single transient error (e.g., ThrottlingException) fails the parity slot as a quality regression because one fabricated flip violates the never-acceptable zero-flip requirement in criterion (b).

The report cannot distinguish fabricated flips from real flips; arms with (A) 3 real flips / 0 errors, (B) 2 real + 1 error, and (C) 0 real / 3 errors produce byte-identical gating strings despite different underlying failure modes.

Adding an errored guard to exclude pairs where a.errored or b.errored from decision_flips and computing a separate errored_pairs metric resolves the double-count and surfaces the distinction in ParityReport.metrics and gating strings.
